gp.text: Gross margin (Revenues less Manufacturing cost of sales as a percentage of Revenues) increased 20 basis points from 44.3% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 to 44.5% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 reflecting product mix.

cor.text: Gross margin (Revenues less Manufacturing cost of sales as a percentage of Revenues) increased 20 basis points from 44.3% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 to 44.5% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 reflecting product mix.

ga.text: Adjusted EBITDA increased $411 from $3,176 for the three months ended September 30, 2025 to $3,587 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 primarily due to higher revenues and improved gross margin partially offset by higher general and administrative expenses.

intro.text: M-tron Industries, Inc. (the "Company," "Mtron," "we," "us," or "our") is engaged in the designing, manufacturing and marketing of highly engineered, high reliability frequency and spectrum control products used to control the frequency or timing of signals in electronic circuits in various applications. Mtron’s primary markets are aerospace & defense, avionics, industrials, and space. Our component-level devices and modules are used extensively in electronic systems for applications in commercial and military defense, aerospace, satellites, down-hole drilling, medical devices, instrumentation, industrial devices and in infrastructure equipment for the telecommunications and network equipment industries.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For the year ended December 31, 2025, our largest and second largest customers accounted for 36.0% and 14.9% of the Company's total revenues, respectively.
Additionally, as of December 31, 2025, four customers accounted for approximately 71.4% of our gross accounts receivable balance.
Additionally, foreign revenues for 2025 (primarily to Malaysia) accounted for 23.2% of our 2025 consolidated revenues.
In 2025 , the Company's largest and second largest customers accounted for $ 19,586 , or 36.0 %, and $ 8,129 , or 14.9 %, respectively, of the Company's total revenues.
In 2024 , the Company's largest and second largest customers accounted for $ 18,145 , or 37.0 %, and $ 8,522 , or 17.4 %, respectively, of the Company’s total revenues.
As of December 31, 2025 , four of the Company's customers accounted for approximately $ 4,898 , or 71.4 %, of gross accounts receivable.
As of December 31, 2024 , four of the Company's customers accounted for approximately $ 4,648 , or 66.2 %, of gross accounts receivable.
Our success depends on our ability to retain key management and technical personnel and attracting, retaining, and training new technical personnel.

If single-source components or key raw materials were to become unavailable on satisfactory terms, and we could not obtain comparable replacement components or raw materials from other sources in a timely manner, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be harmed.
We rely on information technology systems to conduct our business, and disruption, failure or security breaches of these systems could adversely affect our business and results of operations.
We rely on information technology ("IT") systems in order to achieve our business objectives.
We also rely upon industry accepted security measures and technology to securely maintain confidential information maintained on our IT systems.
We rely on third-party providers for cloud infrastructure, hosting, content delivery, telecommunications, and other critical services.

Certain events, including prolonged cloud service disruptions, domain name system failures, payment processor outages, or the insolvency or other failure of a key vendor, may exceed the scope of our business continuity and disaster recovery assumptions and could result in material operational disruption, data loss, reputational harm, and increased costs.
We may also depend on third-party AI models and vendors, and their availability, reliability, performance, or terms of use may change, which could increase costs or negatively affect our operations.

Our ability to generate and maintain sufficient liquidity and capital depends on the profitability of the business, timing of cash flows, general economic conditions and access to the capital markets and the other sources of liquidity and capital described herein.
